annotations.annotation_text: Structural opening of Book 1, Chapter 5, page 125. Continues the multi-layered dream narrative depicting the nocturnal transmigration of human history and Dublin topography.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://jhupbooks.press.jhu.edu/title/annotations-finnegans-wake

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic discourse on page 125: Joyce weaves multilingual puns, etymological roots, and rhythmic cadences capturing the shifting consciousness of the collective unconscious.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: The eternal fraternal dialectic between the opposing sons Shem the Penman (the artist/introvert/outcast) and Shaun the Post (the priest/governor/materialist), embodied in "Shem".
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
